service:
With AWS Lambda Web Functions, you can run web applications and APIs as HTTP servers on AWS Lambda (Lambda) without provisioning or managing servers. Use web functions to run REST APIs, server-rendered web applications, and other HTTP workloads while Lambda handles scaling and availability.

A web function has one or more immutable revisions (code and configuration) and one or more endpoints that expose it over HTTPS.

operations.CreateWebFunction:
Creates a web function with an initial revision and endpoint. To create a web function, you provide the function name, revision configuration (code and service settings), and endpoint configuration.

To use this operation, you must have the CreateWebFunction permission on the web function. You don't need separate permissions for the initial revision or endpoint.
operations.CreateWebFunctionEndpoint:
Creates an endpoint for a web function. An endpoint exposes the web function over HTTPS and routes traffic to one or more revisions.

To use this operation, you must have the CreateWebFunctionEndpoint permission on the web function, not on the endpoint being created.
operations.CreateWebFunctionRevision:
Creates an immutable revision for a web function. A revision represents a specific version of the function code and configuration.

To use this operation, you must have the CreateWebFunctionRevision permission on the web function, not on the revision being created.
operations.DeleteResourcePolicy: Removes the resource-based policy from a web function.
operations.DeleteWebFunction:
Deletes a web function and all of its associated revisions and endpoints.

To use this operation, you must have the DeleteWebFunction permission on the web function. You don't need the DeleteWebFunctionRevision or DeleteWebFunctionEndpoint permission.
operations.DeleteWebFunctionRevision: Deletes a web function revision. You cannot delete a revision that is currently serving traffic on an endpoint.
operations.GetResourcePolicy: Retrieves the resource-based policy attached to a web function.
operations.GetWebAccountSettings: Retrieves details about your AWS Lambda Web Functions account settings for the current AWS Region, including the quotas that apply to web functions and your current usage.
operations.GetWebFunction: Retrieves details about a web function, including its current state and configuration.
operations.GetWebFunctionEndpoint: Retrieves details about a web function endpoint, including its current state, configuration, and domain name.
operations.GetWebFunctionRevision: Retrieves details about a web function revision, including its state and configuration.
operations.ListTags: Returns a list of tags applied to a web function.
operations.ListWebFunctionEndpoints: Lists endpoints for a web function. Use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.
operations.ListWebFunctionRevisions: Lists revisions for a web function. Use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.
operations.ListWebFunctions: Lists web functions in your account. Use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.
operations.PutResourcePolicy: Adds or updates a resource-based policy on a web function. A resource-based policy grants permissions to other AWS accounts or services to perform actions on the web function.
operations.TagResource: Adds tags to a web function. If a tag key already exists, the existing value is overwritten with the new value.
operations.UpdateWebFunctionEndpoint: Updates the configuration of a web function endpoint. You can modify the authorization type, auto-deployment mode, revision weights, scaling, and throttling settings.

ApplicationLogLevel.base:
The log level for application logs. Lambda sends logs at the selected level and at all more severe levels. Possible values, from least to most severe:

  • TRACE – The most detailed information, for tracing code paths.

  • DEBUG – Detailed information for debugging.

  • INFO – General information about application progress.

  • WARN – Potential issues that don't prevent the application from running.

  • ERROR – Errors that prevent an operation from completing.

  • FATAL – Severe errors that cause the application to stop.

refs.LoggingConfig$applicationLogLevel: The log level for application logs emitted by the web function. If you don't specify a value, the default is INFO, and this default is returned in the response.

  • IamAuth – Lambda uses IAM to authorize requests, which must be signed with Signature Version 4 (SigV4).

  • IamAuth – Lambda uses IAM to authorize requests, which must be signed with Signature Version 4 (SigV4).

refs.RegionalEndpoint$authType: The authorization type for the regional endpoint.
refs.UpdateWebFunctionEndpointRequest$authTyp:
The authorization type for the endpoint. Omit this field to keep the current authorization type.

Valid values:

  • ApplicationManaged – Your application handles authorization.

  • IamAuth – Lambda uses IAM to authorize requests, which must be signed with Signature Version 4 (SigV4).

AutoDeploymentMode.base:
The auto-deployment mode for a web function endpoint.

Valid values:

  • LatestRevision – The endpoint automatically serves the newest revision.

  • Disabled – Revision routing stays fixed until you change it.

refs.CreateWebFunctionEndpointRequest$autoDep:
The auto-deployment mode for the endpoint. Controls whether the endpoint automatically serves the newest revision. If you don't specify a value, the default is Disabled, and this default is returned in the response.

Valid values:

  • LatestRevision – The endpoint automatically serves the newest revision.

  • Disabled – Revision routing stays fixed until you change it.

refs.ServiceConfig$egressNetworkConnectorArn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Lambda network connector that gives the web function access to resources in your VPC. You must specify the fully qualified ARN, including the connector version, which pins the revision to that version. If the network connector is deleted, invocations of revisions that reference it fail. Revisions that specify a network connector support only HomeRegion endpoints, not MultiRegion or PerRegion.

refs.ServiceConfig$maxConcurrencyPerEnvironme: The maximum number of concurrent requests handled per execution environment. Minimum value of 1, maximum value of 128. If you don't specify a value, the default is 64, and this default is returned in the response.

refs.ServiceConfig$timeoutSeconds: The amount of time (in seconds) that Lambda allows the web function to run before stopping it. Minimum value of 3, maximum value of 900. If you don't specify a value, the default is 30, and this default is returned in the response.

ServiceQuotaExceededException.base: The request would exceed a service quota, such as the maximum number of web functions in your account or the maximum number of revisions or endpoints per web function. Request a quota increase or reduce usage and try again.

SystemLogLevel.base:
The log level for system logs from the Lambda runtime. Lambda sends logs at the selected level and at all more severe levels. Possible values, from least to most severe:

  • DEBUG – Detailed information about the runtime, for debugging.

  • INFO – General information about the runtime, such as the start and end of execution.

  • WARN – Potential issues detected by the runtime.

refs.LoggingConfig$systemLogLevel: The log level for system logs emitted by the Lambda runtime. If you don't specify a value, the default is INFO, and this default is returned in the response.

refs.UntagResourceRequest$tagKeys: A list of tag keys to remove from the web function.

ThrottleConfig.base: The throttling configuration for a web function endpoint.

refs.CreateWebFunctionEndpointRequest$throttl: The throttling configuration for the endpoint. There is no default value. If you don't specify a throttling configuration, it is absent from the response.
refs.FunctionEndpointSummary$throttleConfig: The throttling configuration for the endpoint. This field is absent if the endpoint has no throttling configuration.
refs.RegionalEndpoint$throttleConfig: The throttling configuration for the regional endpoint. This field is absent if the endpoint has no throttling configuration.
refs.UpdateWebFunctionEndpointRequest$throttl: The throttling configuration for the endpoint. Omit this field to keep the current throttling configuration. To clear a previously set rateLimit value, specify an empty object.

refs.ThrottleConfig$rateLimit: The maximum request rate per second for the endpoint. The value must be one of the following supported values: 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 7000, 8000, 9000, or 10000. The maximum effective value is also bounded by your account-level maximum total rate limit. There is no default value. If you don't specify a value, the throttling configuration is absent from the response. On an update, omit throttleConfig to keep the current value, or specify an empty object to clear a previously set value.

ThrottlingException.base: The request was denied because it exceeded the request rate that Lambda allows for your account. Reduce the frequency of requests and retry with exponential backoff.
